L141.title: Lake claim reliability
L141.hook: A good lake holder almost never lies (99% of calls are true); an evil holder's call is right only ~55% of the time, and an evil "evil" call usually frames a good player

L142.title: Lake Declarer Behavioral Consistency
L142.hook: Roles with enough data all sit at 85–95% consistency, a small spread; "Assassin 100%" rests on 15 cases and is too small a sample to be a rule

L143.title: Assassin Target Seat Preference
L143.hook: Players who led most get hit 49%, those who led least 39%, but lead count is mostly seat rotation, not how active someone is

L136.title: Vote Flip Rate After Team Change
L136.hook: Flip rates differ by only ±1.6pp across roles (Merlin +1.6, Morgana −2.2): far too small to infer a side from

L139.title: Forced P5 Round Outcome Shift

L141.question: When the lake holder announces that the target is evil or good, how often is the target really on that side? Split by first / second / third lake and by the holder's own side.
method: Recomputed every day by generate_cache.py (compute_lake_claim_feature) from every game log in the spreadsheet: this time {{games}} games and {{links}} lake checks, data as of {{date}}.

A lake check is a line "H>T x" in the text record: H is the holder's seat, T the target's seat (0 means seat 10), a trailing x = announced evil, o = announced good, nothing (or ?) = no announcement. Only the first three lake lines of a game count, as the first, second and third lake.
Sides come from the game's role sheet: Assassin, Morgana, Mordred and Oberon are evil, every other role is good.
Reliability = announcements that match the target's real side ÷ announcements in the cell (n).
"By holder" pools the three lakes and splits them by the holder's own side into four cells.
95% intervals are Wilson score intervals (z = 1.96) from the cache; cells with n < {{min}} are flagged as small samples.
Lake lines with no announcement ({{undeclared}} this time) are left out of every cell but counted in the total.
read: "Said evil {{exRate}}% [{{exLo}}–{{exHi}}] n={{exN}}" means: of the {{exN}} times a {{exLakeEn}} holder said evil, the target really was evil {{exRate}}% of the time; the true rate is roughly between {{exLo}}% and {{exHi}}%.

Check the holder's side first: good holders almost always tell the truth; only part of an evil holder's announcements are true, and an evil holder calling someone evil is usually framing a good player (see "By holder").

The per-lake numbers mix good and evil holders: the more evil holders, the lower the overall reliability. Differences between lakes mostly reflect who holds the lake, not a person changing how they announce.
caveats: The Lady of the Lake shows the holder the target's real side, so an announcement that does not match is almost always a lie; a few may be typos in the record.
By the rules the next holder is the previous target, so second and third holders are in effect chosen by the previous holder, and their good / evil mix differs from the first lake.
Game logs are typed by hand: a missing mark is left out, a wrong mark is counted.
These are averages over all players, not any one player; individual habits can differ a lot.

L142.question: After announcing a lake result, does the holder pick teams that match the announcement when they lead? Does the consistency rate differ by role?
method: One-off study: the original report {{source}} lives on the owner's PC, not in the repository; scripts/build_feature_studies.py wrote its numbers into the cache: a {{games}}-game snapshot, {{links}} lake checks, {{leaderEvents}} teams picked by a holder who had announced a lake result.
The daily update does not recompute these numbers; generate_cache.py (annotate_feature_studies) only rewrites the conclusion from them and flags cells with n < {{min}} as small samples.

One event = one team picked by a holder who had announced; a pick that matches the announcement is "consistent", otherwise "inconsistent" (the report's Section 2 "leader picks alignment"; the typical inconsistency is calling someone evil and then putting them on the team).
Consistency = consistent ÷ (consistent + inconsistent), n = events for the role; the role is the holder's own role.

High-EV cells: among the combinations role × announced evil / good × consistent or not, the {{cellCount}} whose games ended 3-red furthest from the baseline (3-red rate over all games of the snapshot, {{baseline}}%); Δ 3-red = the group's 3-red rate − baseline.
95% intervals are computed by the site: consistency from consistent / total; high-EV cells from the 3-red rate × n back to a count, then the Wilson method (z = 1.96).
read: Read n and the interval first: roles with enough data differ little and their intervals overlap; roles with n < {{min}} (including the 100% cell) have very wide intervals and show no pattern.
An inconsistency is worth a question but does not identify a side on its own.
Treat the high-EV cells as hints only: they are the extremes picked from many cells and will most likely shrink with new data.
caveats: Only holders who later lead produce events; evil holders rarely lead afterwards, so almost every evil role is a small sample.
The high-EV cells are the largest gaps picked from all combinations, mostly with small n: picking extremes exaggerates them (multiple comparisons).
Δ 3-red is a correlation, not a cause: consistency and how the game is going affect each other.
One-off study: the numbers stay at the {{games}}-game snapshot and do not follow the daily update.

L143.question: When the Assassin shoots after 3-blue, is the target related to how often they led or where they sat? Does the chance of hitting Merlin change with that?
method: One-off study: the original report {{source}} is not in the repository; scripts/build_feature_studies.py wrote it into the cache: a {{games}}-game snapshot, {{attempts}} assassinations. The daily update does not recompute the numbers; generate_cache.py only rewrites the conclusion from them.
Hit rate = shots whose target really was Merlin ÷ shots in the group (n); missed = 100% − hit rate.

Leader tiers: shots are split by how many times the target led in that game into most / middle / least (cut points as in the original report; the site cannot verify them); the three tiers add up to {{tierTotal}} shots.
The seat table splits by the target's seat; the cache only keeps the {{seatCount}} seats with the highest hit rate, the others are not provided.
95% intervals are computed by the site from hit rate × n back to a count, then the Wilson method (z = 1.96); n < {{min}} is flagged as a small sample.
read: Hit rate is "how often the Assassin was right when choosing this kind of player", not "how often this kind of player gets chosen".
The most-led tier has a higher hit rate, but check whether the intervals overlap first; and how often someone leads is mostly seat rotation (who starts, how many rounds), not how active they are.
To find Merlin, read what people say and how they vote, not their lead count or seat.
caveats: The seat table lists only the top seats: listing the highest ones overstates the gap, and the seats left out may be about the same (selection bias).
Lead count is tied to seat and game length (longer games give everyone more leads): a confounder.
One-off study: the numbers stay at the {{games}}-game snapshot and do not follow the daily update.

L136.question: After the team changes, do players change their vote (approve to reject or back)? Do good, evil and each role flip at different rates?
method: One-off study: the original report {{source}} is not in the repository; scripts/build_feature_studies.py wrote it into the cache: a {{games}}-game snapshot, {{chances}} vote chances. The daily update does not recompute the numbers; generate_cache.py only rewrites the conclusion from them.
From the study's name: a chance = one player's vote after the team changed, a flip = that vote differs from their vote on the previous team (about {{perPlayerGame}} chances per player per game).
Overall flip rate by side (cache summary): good {{blue}}%, evil {{red}}%, a {{delta}}pp gap.

Each role also has two flip columns (cache fields flipRedPct / flipBluePct, labelled red / blue); how the two are split is only in the original report and the site cannot confirm it, so they are labelled by field name.
signed EV = flip % (blue) − flip % (red) (the cache's numbers check out), in points; the original study reads a positive value as a "good signal".
No interval: a player's several votes in one game are not independent, so the {{chances}} chances cannot be treated as independent samples.
read: Roles' signed EV fall within {{span}}pp; the sides differ by only {{delta}}pp overall.
A player has about {{perPlayerGame}} chances per game, so a {{delta}}pp gap is about {{perGameDiff}} more or fewer flips per game: impossible to tell at the table.
Do not infer a side from a changed vote.
caveats: A "flip" ignores direction and reason (who was swapped in or out); averaging different situations can cancel out.
The sample is large, so such a small gap may be statistically real, but it is of little practical use.
One-off study: the numbers stay at the {{games}}-game snapshot and do not follow the daily update.

L139.question: In games where a round's mission went all the way to the fifth proposal (P5, forced), do the three endings come out differently from other games?
method: One-off study: the original report {{source}} is not in the repository; scripts/build_feature_studies.py wrote it into the cache: a {{games}}-game snapshot. The daily update does not recompute the numbers; generate_cache.py only rewrites the conclusion from them.

P5 = the fifth proposal of a round: when the first four teams are all rejected, the fifth goes on the mission without a vote (forced). "P5 in R3" = games whose third mission went to the fifth proposal.

3-red rate = share of these games that ended 3-red; baseline {{baseline}}% = the 3-red rate over all games of the snapshot. Δ 3-red / Δ 3-blue dead / Δ 3-blue alive = the group's share of that ending − the share over all games (points); the three add up to about 0.
"With / without P5 in R3" splits all games in two: {{withN}} + {{withoutN}} = {{games}} games.

R1 is left out: almost every game reaches P5 in R1, so there is no comparison group (the report attributes it to padding in the spreadsheet import; in this community the first four R1 proposals are also often "talk teams" that never go on a mission).
95% intervals are computed by the site from the 3-red rate × n back to a count, then the Wilson method (z = 1.96); n < {{min}} is flagged as a small sample.
read: This is a conditional rate: among games reaching P5 in R3, 3-red differs from the baseline by {{r3delta}}pp. It only says these games end 3-red at a different frequency, not that reaching P5 makes evil stronger.
R4 and R5 have few games ({{r4n}} and {{r5n}}) and wide intervals: check whether the interval covers the baseline before reading the gap.
caveats: Selection bias: rejecting all the way to P5 is itself the result of a game already tilting evil (good cannot control the table); P5 is a symptom of a bad position, not the cause, and not evidence of evil cover.
One-off study: the numbers stay at the {{games}}-game snapshot and do not follow the daily update.
L139.baselineNow: The {{baseline}}% baseline is the 3-red rate of the study's snapshot; the current cache's 3-red rate over all games is {{currentThreeRed}}% (different snapshot and filters), so the two cannot be subtracted directly.

finalWinRate.name: Final win rate
finalWinRate.def: Share of games won in the end (assassination included).
finalWinRate.calc: Wins ÷ games. Red wins = three failed missions, or three successes and Merlin assassinated; Blue wins = three successes and Merlin survives.
finalWinRate.meaning: The plain win rate, but it depends on the roles drawn: red roles win more often.

expectedWinRate.name: Expected win rate
expectedWinRate.def: The final win rate an average player would have with the roles you drew.
expectedWinRate.calc: Σ (your games as a role × everyone's average final win rate in that role) ÷ your games.
expectedWinRate.meaning: A baseline: a player who drew more red roles has a higher expected win rate.

excessWinRate.name: Excess win rate
excessWinRate.def: How much more (or less) you win than an average player once role-draw luck is removed.
excessWinRate.calc: Final win rate − expected win rate (percentage points). The expected rate uses everyone's average win rate in each role, weighted by your games in that role.
excessWinRate.meaning: +5 = with the same roles you win 5 points more than average; 0 = average; negative = below average. Noisy with few games.

redWinRate.name: Red win rate
redWinRate.def: Final win rate when on Red (Assassin, Morgana, Mordred, Oberon).
redWinRate.calc: Red wins (three fails + Merlin assassinated) ÷ games on Red.
redWinRate.meaning: Red's average is high; compare with other players' red rates, not with blue rates.

blueWinRate.name: Blue win rate
blueWinRate.def: Final win rate when on Blue (Merlin, Percival, Loyal Servants).
blueWinRate.calc: Blue wins (three successes and Merlin survives) ÷ games on Blue.
blueWinRate.meaning: Blue's average is low; compare with other players' blue rates.

roleTheory.name: Role-theory win rate
roleTheory.def: Your expected win rate if every role were drawn at its standard rate.
roleTheory.calc: Σ draw probability × your final win rate in the role (10 players: Loyal 4/10, the other six roles 1/10 each). A role with too few games uses the population average.
roleTheory.meaning: Removes role-draw luck: how well you play each role.

positionTheory.name: Position-theory win rate
positionTheory.def: Your expected win rate if every seat came up equally often.
positionTheory.calc: Σ 1/10 × your final win rate in seat 1–10. A seat with too few games uses the population average.
positionTheory.meaning: Removes seat luck: how well you play from each seat.

overallTheory.name: Overall-theory win rate
overallTheory.def: Your expected win rate if roles and seats were both drawn at their standard rates.
overallTheory.calc: Σ role draw probability × 1/10 × your final win rate in that role × seat cell. With 7 × 10 cells most players lack games in many cells; those use the population average.
overallTheory.meaning: The most complete in theory, but often short of data; the more cells filled in, the closer it stays to average.

missionWinRate.name: Mission win rate
missionWinRate.def: Share of games your side won the mission phase (before the assassination).
missionWinRate.calc: On Blue: games that reached three successes; on Red: games that reached three failures.
missionWinRate.meaning: Team picks, votes and mission cards, without the assassination.

assassinWinRate.name: Assassination win rate
assassinWinRate.def: After three successful missions, the share your side won the assassination.
assassinWinRate.calc: Three-success games only. On Blue: Merlin survived ÷ those games; on Red: Merlin hit ÷ those games.
assassinWinRate.meaning: Blue: hiding Merlin; Red: finding Merlin. Fewer games count, so n is shown.

coWin.name: Won / lost together
coWin.def: Games the two played on one team and won (or lost).
coWin.calc: A count. If both won the same game, they were on the same team.
coWin.meaning: Mostly how often the two play and share a team.

winCorr.name: When I win, so do they
winCorr.def: Of my wins, the share where they won too.
winCorr.calc: Won together ÷ my total wins × 100%. Not a correlation coefficient, so never negative; row = me, column = them, and the two directions differ.
winCorr.meaning: A high value mostly means they often share my team; see Net chemistry for chemistry.

coWinMinusLose.name: Net chemistry
coWinMinusLose.def: On my team, do they win with me more or lose with me more?
coWinMinusLose.calc: "When I win, so do they" minus "when I lose, so do they" (percentage points).
coWinMinusLose.meaning: Positive = we win together more often; negative = we lose together more often. How often we share a team cancels out.

lakeTruth.name: Truthful lake claims
lakeTruth.def: Share of Lady of the Lake claims that matched the target's real side.
lakeTruth.calc: Matching claims ÷ claims made, Blue and Red together.
lakeTruth.meaning: Blue almost always tells the truth; lying is normal for Red, so players often on Red score lower.

anomalyVote.name: Off-pattern votes
anomalyVote.def: Votes against the usual pattern: approving a team you're not on, or rejecting a team you're on.
anomalyVote.meaning: Higher = less conventional voting; it can carry information or be random.

topRoleWinRate.name: Best-role win rate
topRoleWinRate.def: Final win rate in your best role.
topRoleWinRate.calc: The highest final win rate among roles with at least 3 games.
topRoleWinRate.meaning: How strong your best role is.

outcomeMix.name: Game result (share within share)
outcomeMix.def: How their games split into three fails / three successes + Merlin hit / three successes + Merlin alive; each part is split again into won (solid) and lost (striped).
outcomeMix.calc: Three fails = on Red (won) + on Blue (lost); Merlin hit = on Red (won) + on Blue (lost); Merlin alive = on Blue (won) + on Red (lost). Each ÷ their games.
outcomeMix.meaning: The solid parts add up to the final win rate. More stripes in a part = they often lose that kind of ending.

chiSquare.name: p-value (is the gap luck?)
chiSquare.def: If the grouping (say, the seat) had no effect at all, the chance that luck alone would produce a gap this large.
chiSquare.calc: Chi-square test: work out how many games each cell should have if the grouping did not matter, add up how far the real counts are from that (χ²), and turn it into a probability p.
chiSquare.meaning: p below 0.05: luck rarely makes a gap this big, so the gap is real. p above 0.05: the gap could be luck. p says whether a gap is real, not why.

threeRedRate.name: Three-fail rate
threeRedRate.def: Share of these games Red won on missions (three failed missions).
threeRedRate.calc: Three-fail games ÷ games in the group.
threeRedRate.meaning: Higher = Blue struggles to pass missions in this situation. Blue's mission win rate = 100% − this.

killRate.name: Hit rate
killRate.def: After three successful missions, the share where the assassin hit Merlin.
killRate.calc: Merlin hit ÷ (Merlin hit + Merlin alive). Three-success games only, n = those games; three-fail games have no assassination.
killRate.meaning: Higher = Merlin is easier to spot in this situation. Merlin survival = 100% − hit rate.

redGameWinRate.name: Red win rate (whole game)
redGameWinRate.def: Share of these games Red won in the end: three fails, or three successes and Merlin hit.
redGameWinRate.calc: (Three fails + Merlin hit) ÷ games in the group.
redGameWinRate.meaning: Blue win rate = 100% − this = Merlin alive ÷ games.

missionSuccessRate.name: Mission success rate
missionSuccessRate.def: Of the games that reached this mission, the share where it succeeded (Blue).
missionSuccessRate.calc: Games where this mission succeeded ÷ games that reached it. Success follows the rules: with 7+ players mission 4 needs two fail cards to fail.
missionSuccessRate.meaning: Lower = Red breaks this mission more often.

failCards.name: Fail cards
failCards.def: How many fail cards came out on this mission.
failCards.calc: Games with 0 / 1 / 2+ fail cards ÷ games that reached the mission.
failCards.meaning: 2+ = at least two Red players on the team both failed it. On mission 4 (7+ players) a single fail card still lets it succeed.

captainFaction.name: Leader's side
captainFaction.def: For the team that actually went on each mission, whether its leader was Red or Blue.
captainFaction.calc: Games with a Red (or Blue) leader ÷ games that reached the mission.
captainFaction.meaning: Red leaders tend to put Red players on the team, so their missions fail more often.

firstProposal.def: The first team proposal for the first mission.
firstProposal.calc: Whether Merlin / Percival was on that team and how many Red players it had, then how those games ended — whether or not the 1-1 team actually went.
firstProposal.meaning: At 1-1 nobody has information yet, so this shows whether the team make-up is linked to the result.

missionPath.name: Mission path
missionPath.def: The order in which missions succeeded or failed, e.g. fail-fail-pass-pass-pass.
missionPath.calc: Each game's real mission results in order; games with the same path are counted together.
missionPath.meaning: The path decides three fails or three successes; for three successes look at the assassination.

lakeCombo.name: Holder → target
lakeCombo.def: For this Lady of the Lake: which side held the Lake and which side they checked.
lakeCombo.calc: Four groups by the two players' real sides; missions, assassination and whole-game results for each.
lakeCombo.meaning: Shows how who holds and who gets checked relates to the result — a link, not proof the Lake helps either side.

evilTeamReject.name: Team with Red → reject
evilTeamReject.def: Share of votes rejecting a proposed team that has at least one Red player.
evilTeamReject.calc: Reject votes on such teams ÷ all votes on them (proposals 1–4, both sides' votes).
evilTeamReject.meaning: Higher = teams with Red get blocked more often. Red players vote too, so it never reaches 100%.

goodTeamApprove.name: All-Blue team → approve
goodTeamApprove.def: Share of votes approving a proposed team that is all Blue.
goodTeamApprove.calc: Approve votes on such teams ÷ all votes on them (proposals 1–4).
goodTeamApprove.meaning: Higher = good teams pass more easily. Red often rejects them, and Blue can't always tell.

r3Reject.name: Rejects from mission 3
r3Reject.def: From mission 3 on, the share of this side's votes that were rejections (whatever the team).
r3Reject.calc: Reject votes ÷ all votes, proposals 1–4 of missions 3+; Loyal Servants and Red counted separately.
r3Reject.meaning: Compares how Loyal Servants and Red players vote.

flipRate.name: Flip rate
flipRate.def: After a team changes, the share of votes that differ from the same player's vote on the previous team.
flipRate.calc: Flips ÷ votes after a team change (one-off study, numbers frozen at its snapshot).
flipRate.meaning: The two columns are the same role under the study's two groupings; see the full study.

signedEv.name: Flip gap (signed EV)
signedEv.def: The difference between a role's two flip-rate columns.
signedEv.calc: Flip rate (Blue) − flip rate (Red), in percentage points.
signedEv.meaning: The study read positive values as a 'Blue signal', but roles differ by only about ±2 points — too small to notice at the table.
